clue.text: Jersey policeman's order to erring motorist

definitions.meaning: the instruction to steer to the kerb and stop

explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted sweater, and a traffic officer tells a speeding driver to halt at the roadside.

clue.text: Said you do wrong going back on agreement

indicators.note: said means the word you is spoken, giving the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: you said aloud is the letter U

indicators.note: going back means the word for do wrong is read from right to left

parts.note: to do wrong is to sin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accuses another of backsliding on a deal they had made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns SIN into NIS, set after U (the letter that sounds like 'you').
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in complete accord, so the word is a synonym of harmony.

clue.text: Those who aren't priests have a song about it

indicators.note: about means the song word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers are told they have a hymn on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IT inside LAY, an old word for a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are the ordinary members of a church as opposed to its clergy.

clue.text: Guard got advance payment after night service

indicators.note: after means the payment piece comes behind the service piece

parts.note: a vigil is a nighttime religious watch or service
an ante is a stake put up in advance, as in poker

explanation.surface: A security man was paid up front after attending a late church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a self-appointed protector who keeps watch and enforces order unofficially.

clue.text: To stir mixture round in a dish

indicators.note: mixture means the letters of to stir are mixed up

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to stir the mixture round in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges TOSTIR into RISOTT, and the ring-shaped O finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice preparation, served as a plate of food.

clue.text: Lying girl grabs ornamental brooch

indicators.note: grabs means the girl's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
a pin is a decorative clasp worn on clothing

explanation.surface: A dishonest girl snatches a decorative brooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like 'telling untruths' but means lying flat on one's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means reclining face upward, stretched out flat.

clue.text: Puts down something found in pen on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the ship abbreviation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: board here suggests a vessel, and SS stands for steamship
a fountain pen holds ink

explanation.surface: An odd riddle about what one might find in a pen while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for 'inside SS', the steamship abbreviation, so INK goes between the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink something is to lower it or send it to the bottom, as when a golfer holes a putt.

clue.text: Write about one teacher, a senior citizen

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: about means the teacher word goes around the number word

parts.note: Sir is how a schoolboy addresses a male teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone composes a piece about a teacher, now an elderly retiree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ONE inside SIR, giving SIONER after PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner draws a retirement income, so is typically an elderly person past working age.

clue.text: Name and number a friend takes home

indicators.note: takes means the friend word swallows the home word

parts.note: a mate is a friend
in means at home

explanation.surface: A request for a name and phone number, about a friend's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' puts IN inside MATE after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put forward their name as a candidate.

clue.text: Working underground for 30 seconds in Gateshead

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and MIN is the first half of that word
taken as written
the head, or first letter, of Gateshead is G

explanation.surface: A half-minute stint below ground in a town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England near Newcastle, an old coal area; its 'head' is the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining is extracting coal or ore from beneath the earth.

clue.text: What you're seeking is city my son's going around

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the city abbreviation
going means the letters of my son's are moving, so rearranged

parts.note: the letters of my son's, including the S
NY is short for New York City

explanation.surface: Someone tells a searcher that the city is what their boy is touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' rearranges MYSONS into SYNOMS, and 'around' puts NY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Most cryptic definitions ask for another word meaning the same, so a solver hunts for equivalent words.

clue.text: College understood about student speaking several languages

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a type of college

indicators.note: about means the word for understood goes around the student letter

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so understood is got
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A college student understood to be fluent in many tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside GOT after POLY (a polytechnic, a former type of British college).
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot person can use many tongues, from Greek for many and tongue.

clue.text: Going downhill fast?

parts.note: reads like declining rapidly, but means descending a snowy slope on runners

explanation.definitionFit: Skiers glide down mountain slopes at speed, so the sport is quick descent.

clue.text: Time to thump record buyer!

parts.note: ten is a time, ten o'clock
to pound is to hit hard
to note is to record

explanation.surface: A command that now is the moment to batter a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: A ten-pound note is a British banknote, which buys things, hence 'buyer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is money, which is the means of purchasing goods.

clue.text: Malta, best place to see coasters

indicators.note: place means the letters are put into a new position

explanation.surface: Malta is recommended as the top spot for seeing coastal vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' rearranges MALTA BEST; 'coasters' looks like ships but means table protectors.
explanation.definitionFit: Coasters are small mats protecting a table surface from glasses and dishes.

clue.text: Send Ken as upset by nudity

indicators.note: upset means the letters of send Ken as are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ken is sent off because someone is upset by his lack of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity and nakedness both describe being without clothing.

clue.text: Turns to let someone in

parts.note: reads like a person who relents, but describes a handle rotated to open an entrance

explanation.definitionFit: A round handle is twisted to release the latch and open the entrance.

clue.text: Bloke reduced journeys by bus

indicators.note: journeys means the letters travel about and land in new places

explanation.surface: A man who cut down on his trips by public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journeys' rearranges BLOKE REDUCED; a double-decker is a two-level bus, a London icon.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker is a two-storey passenger vehicle, the classic red London type.

clue.text: Having refined upbringing man broke out

indicators.note: in a down clue upbringing means the word is brought up, read bottom to top

parts.note: refined means pure
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man with a genteel upbringing escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' turns PURE into ERUP, ahead of TED.
explanation.definitionFit: When a volcano erupts it bursts forth, so the word means burst out suddenly.

clue.text: Jack takes milk supplier's jar

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
a cow's udder supplies milk

explanation.surface: Jack picks up the milkman's jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container but is a verb, to jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To judder is to shake violently, which is to jolt or jar.

clue.text: Mourn the first girl I ever danced with

indicators.note: the first signals the opening letter of the word girl
danced with means the letters of I ever move about and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone laments the first girl they ever danced with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'danced with' rearranges I EVER into RIEVE, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to feel deep sorrow over a loss, as a bereaved person does.

clue.text: Died after dash to find animal

indicators.note: after means the died letter follows the dash word

parts.note: dash in the sense of verve or flair is elan

explanation.surface: Someone perished after rushing off to find a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' suggests rushing but means style.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope, a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: To get less than one's share is a blow

parts.note: under means below or less than
a cut is a portion of the proceeds

explanation.surface: Being short-changed on one's portion is a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' looks like a misfortune but is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing an undercut is a punch thrown upward from below, a type of strike.

clue.text: Jewish leader held in Arab bivouac

indicators.note: held in means the answer is contained within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A Jewish leader is detained at an Arab camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a teacher and religious head of a Jewish congregation.

clue.text: Unusually thin man swallowed medicinal preparation

indicators.note: swallowed means the shuffled letters take in the man's name
unusually means the letters of thin are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A strangely skinny fellow gulped down some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges THIN into INHT, and 'swallowed' puts ALAN inside it after INH; 'man' is a name, not the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhalant is a remedy breathed in as vapour, such as for clearing congestion.

clue.text: Include stiff compiler, rejected at first

indicators.note: at first means the turned piece comes in front
rejected means the compiler's word is turned back to front

parts.note: the setter, or compiler, refers to himself as me
a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a rigid setter, turned down at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ME into EM; 'stiff' is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody is to contain or incorporate something as a part.

clue.text: Lowered when in a bed!

indicators.note: in means the word for when sits inside the bed word

parts.note: taken as written
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who feels lower when lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AS inside BED, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase is to humble or degrade, bringing someone down in status.

clue.text: Rise after tossing in bed of bundles of papers

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the bed word

parts.note: doss is slang for a makeshift bed or a sleep

indicators.note: tossing means the letters of rise are thrown about

explanation.surface: Getting up after tossing and turning in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing' rearranges RISE into SIER, and 'in' puts it inside DOSS (British slang for a rough bed).
explanation.definitionFit: Dossiers are collections of documents on a person or subject, kept in files.
